correctness.rationale: For zero-cost single uniform price p>=0 and two positive exponential valuation-class weights, R′>0 for p<=1/k and R′<0 for p>=1. Within (1/k,1), R′ has sign w/(1-w)-H_k(p). The exact log derivative of H has sign kp²-(k+1)p+2, with positive discriminant only for k>3+2sqrt2; two extrema of H then produce precisely 1 or 3 stationary prices, and folded tangent roots do not add strict local maxima. The two peak revenues have strictly increasing log ratio in w because the envelope derivative is strictly increasing in price. One peak dominates at each fold, so a unique equal-height w*(k) lies strictly inside; both separated prices are global maxima there. Boundary k=k_c is monotone despite derivative zero. This is an analytic continuum classification, not inferred from a k=10 numerical example.
